# m.options.open_interest_by_underlying

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Each underlying's open interest at the end of each trading day, calls and puts split out.

Call it from a session `m`, made with `dm.MassiveSession()`:

```python
m.options.open_interest_by_underlying(symbols=None, *, start=None, end=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None, on_error=None)
```

- [Methods](README.md#query-methods): `fetch()`, `poll(interval)`
- Read from: REST
- `poll()` by default: `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`, which holds only the latest poll's rows, one row per `Symbol` and `Date`

[Dataset index](README.md)

## Arguments

A linked argument follows its rule under [shared arguments](README.md#shared-arguments) on the dataset index.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`symbols`](README.md#symbols) | Stock, ETF, or index tickers, such as `"AAPL"` or `"I:SPX"`; leave it out for every underlying. |
| [`start`](README.md#start) | The first trading day. |
| [`end`](README.md#end) | The last trading day. |
| [`sort`](README.md#sort) | Any of Massive's field names, such as `"open_interest"`. Fields: any REST field under [Massive fields](#massive-fields). |
| [`order`](README.md#order) | The direction of `sort`. |
| [`limit`](README.md#limit) | The most rows to return, in total. A watchlist's `fetch()` caps every request instead. |
| [`filters`](README.md#filters) | Further endpoint parameters, such as `{"underlying_ticker_gte": "A"}`. Keys: `underlying_ticker_gt`, `underlying_ticker_gte`, `underlying_ticker_lt`, `underlying_ticker_lte`. |
| [`on_error`](README.md#on_error) | What a bad symbol or row does in this call (`dm.ErrorPolicy`). None, the default, takes each cause from the session's `MassiveConfig.on_error`. |

## Plans

How recent the data is on each of Massive's plans, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Open Interest by Underlying (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Options Basic | Not included |
| Options Starter | Not included |
| Options Developer | Not included |
| Options Advanced | End-of-day, All history |
| Options Business | Not included |
| Historical Options Analytics Business | End-of-day, All history |

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The row's instrument, as Massive's ticker. From REST `underlying_ticker`: "The ticker of the underlying (e.g., SPX). Totals cover every root on the underlying, so weekly roots (SPXW) and roots adjusted after a corporate action (AMCR1) are included." The underlying, with its `I:` prefix for an index (`I:SPX`), as in `m.options.contracts()`. If Massive's [All Contracts](https://massive.com/docs/rest/options/contracts/all-contracts) list can't say whether a ticker is an index, the library leaves its rows out and lists them in `m.problems()` as `unreadable_symbols`. A ticker that names both a stock and an index (`DJT`) is classified by the first contract Massive lists for it, and the library can't tell whether Massive's row counts the stock's options, the index's, or both. A watchlist gets a row only under the spelling the library gives it: its row under the other spelling is left out, as an `unrequested_symbols` problem. |
| `Date` | String | The trading date the open interest applies to (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `OpenInterest` | long | Total open interest across every contract on the underlying. |
| `OpenInterestCalls` | long | Total open interest across the underlying's call contracts. |
| `OpenInterestPuts` | long | Total open interest across the underlying's put contracts. |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, by the local clock. Rows that arrive together share it. It isn't Massive's time, and later rows can carry earlier times. In a `poll()` table, it's the time of the poll the row's values came from. |
